title: libpod: trigger autofs with Statx before bind-mounting volumes
body:
Currently, bind-mount checks use `stat`, `fstatat`, or `statfs`, which don't trigger autofs mounts. Because of this, starting a container can fail if the share hasn't been accessed on the host first.

This change adds a `unix.Statx()` call without AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT in `generateSpec` to trigger the mount before the bind mount is processed. For FreeBSD, the function is a no-op.

Reference: https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-96072?actionerId=70121%3Ab4f0c4b7-8565-491a-a859-6d13a8670279&sourceType=assign

#### How tested

Autofs is not set up in CI, so this was verified manually on a host with a direct autofs map.

Setup used

- Map file /etc/auto.podman-test:
  /mnt/podman-autofs -fstype=none,bind :/var/tmp/podman-autofs-source
- Source directory contained a known file (hello.txt).
- Built binary from this branch (./bin/podman), with isolated --root / --runroot so the run did not depend on the system store.

Procedure

1. Make sure /mnt/podman-autofs is dormant: findmnt -R /mnt/podman-autofs should show a single autofs entry (no covering bind/NFS yet). If a covering mount is still present, wait for the map idle timeout or unmount it (may need root), then check again.
2. Confirm that a normal "no automount" lookup does not wake the share: statx with AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT on /mnt/podman-autofs leaves findmnt unchanged (still only autofs).
3. Do not access the path beforehand (ls, cat, etc. would wake autofs and invalidate the test).
4. Run:
   ./bin/podman --root … --runroot … run --rm -v /mnt/podman-autofs:/data:z alpine cat /data/hello.txt
5. Expected result: the command prints the contents of hello.txt, and afterward findmnt shows a covering mount on /mnt/podman-autofs (the share was triggered during container setup).

comments.body: I Agree a test would be nice though I am not sure how viable this is due the external autofs setup required. I guess in the CI VMs we could configure some static dummy mounts? Otherwise please at least document how this was tested end to end.
Does this fix an issue that's been filed?  If so, please add a link to the description @veronnicka

> Does this fix an issue that's been filed? If so, please add a link to the description @veronnicka

I didnt find it, I believe there is only the rhel ticket, I can link that

Looking at this I think I could need some more clarification. I sssume we are talking about autofs here. How does this compare to systemd automount units, are they affected the same way or not? If not could we just tell the user to use the systemd automount functionality?
Otherwise what is missing here then is why do they do not want to stat the path themselves before hand. Like for example we still to this day refuse to create the source directory of a bind mount as we say the user must take care of this, why is auto mounting different in that regard? The user would need to make sure to mount there path before hand.

> Looking at this I think I could need some more clarification. I sssume we are talking about autofs here. How does this compare to systemd automount units, are they affected the same way or not? If not could we just tell the user to use the systemd automount functionality? Otherwise what is missing here then is why do they do not want to stat the path themselves before hand. Like for example we still to this day refuse to create the source directory of a bind mount as we say the user must take care of this, why is auto mounting different in that regard? The user would need to make sure to mount there path before hand.

If I understand it correctly, systemd automount still sets up an autofs mountpoint https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/6cdf9c9b46ecd061ccfbf77b2841adb59a4b3831/src/core/automount.c#L698. So switching to systemd automount does not avoid the AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT issue.

As for whether users should just trigger the mount themselves beforehand: that is a fair question. My understanding is the decision was to move forward with doing this automatically in Podman; context is in the RHEL ticket: https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-96072?actionerId=70121%3Ab4f0c4b7-8565-491a-a859-6d13a8670279&sourceType=assign

> I Agree a test would be nice though I am not sure how viable this is due the external autofs setup required. I guess in the CI VMs we could configure some static dummy mounts? Otherwise please at least document how this was tested end to end.

the steps are documented now in the description.

@Luap99 I don't think rejecting an entire system of automounting because a newer version exists is a valid reason to reject. Autofs existed for years before systemd did, and expecting folks to migrate immediately because we'd prefer to support just one is not a viable option.

> @Luap99 I don't think rejecting an entire system of automounting because a newer version exists is a valid reason to reject. Autofs existed for years before systemd did, and expecting folks to migrate immediately because we'd prefer to support just one is not a viable option.

Well its not that I want to reject this. But if we were to add an opt in option what is the point then? At that point the users should just trigger the mounts themselves before calling podman IMO.

For systemd wise I am asking because I liked to know how that one works not that I rejected autofs per se. I am asking because the systemd dependencies are designed to trivially map all these relationships. Because we recommend using quadlets for running containers one could easily use RequiresMountFor= there which should trigger the mount AFAIK then. Though I suppose this wont work for rootless units.
Based on the discussion at the community meeting, I'll proceed without adding a new `autofs` option. I'll also work on adding an integration test to cover this scenario.
